findings_fixed.identified_by: independent release_audit reviewer; confirmed by parent and core
findings_fixed.problem: The previous _refs implementation parses source_refs separately inside each span loop. Reusing a single parsed ref with a shallow dictionary copy introduced cross-span sharing of ordinary message_indices lists and arbitrary nested JSON containers. Serialized outputs could remain equal while mutating one returned reference changed another.
findings_fixed.fix_verified: The final fast path requires exactly one ordinary span and consumes a matching captured page map at most once. Multi-span and repeated-page cases call the original _refs path, retaining its independent parses and object graphs. No deepcopy, new cache or row-private key was introduced.

findings_fixed.problem: A custom breadcrumb can replace row.id with a list before reference projection; a new captured_refs lookup would then add a TypeError that the old reference method did not raise.
findings_fixed.fix_verified: Reference reuse requires an exact native-str current row id, after the original breadcrumb call. Other ids retain the original reference-method call and downstream behavior.

findings_fixed.problem: Capturing whichever json.loads callable was present at import could certify a wrapper installed before store import. Its per-call effects must remain observable.
findings_fixed.fix_verified: Initial certification requires a native Python function with ordinary json module/name/qualname/code-name and matching json source-file origin. Unknown origins produce None, retaining every original parse. Current loader identity is checked again at reuse.

reviewed_invariants: The source-turn relation is built only inside the original recall read transaction. Every original source-map and projected-unit check still runs with the same selected pages, parsed reference values and exact original-turn text.

Batching accepts only an exact sqlite3.Connection with native Row/str factories, ordinary source preparation, at least two nonempty sessions, native-str keys and signed-64-bit native-int ordinal sets. Boolean, mixed, overflow, custom and excessive inputs return to the unchanged original per-session loop before sorting or binding.

At most 400 requested pairs and 800 parameters are bound. Actual variable and ASCII SQL-length limits are checked. Restrictive column/expression/compound/VM limits and absent getlimit retain the original path; no limits are raised, queries chunked or SQL errors swallowed.

The parameterized VALUES relation uses the existing unique session_pk/ordinal lookup. The comparison places native turns columns on the same affinity-bearing side as the legacy predicates. Selecting requested_turns.session_pk retains the original requested dictionary key; missing turns remain absent for the original validator to handle.

The standard prepare_source_units identity is an optimization guard, not a replacement for source integrity checks. Custom preparation preserves the old per-session reads and fresh reference projection.

Reference capture is confined to the current recall and exact raw source_refs object. The final current _refs/JSON loader/row/id/span guards run after breadcrumb construction. Late mutations, empty or malformed spans and unsupported row types retain the original call and parse/error behavior.

Single-span reference clipping preserves the old nested loop order, comparisons, offsets and fresh outer dictionaries. A captured graph is exposed at most once, preserving nested message_indices/extra-container independence across output references.

No private key is inserted into rows, assembly inputs, breadcrumbs or returned results. No query/result/statement cache or new database schema is introduced by C6. The previously registered bounded token-count memo and connection-local pager remain unchanged.
The original character path, semantic/coverage routing, custom methods, rank ordering, result counts, complete payload shape and named-tokenizer exact counts are not intentionally changed.

limits: Static inspection and targeted tests do not prove all possible program executions. Certification does not attempt to detect deliberate forgery or mutation of private module code/decoder internals and matching origin metadata.
Python 3.10 deliberately retains the legacy SQL path because sqlite3.Connection.getlimit is unavailable; this review does not claim the new batch optimization runs on every supported interpreter.
